FOUNDER DIRECTIVE (Samuel, 2026-09-09) relayed verbatim in intent by Fable; A and B copied so A's database review and staging rehearsal start NOW in parallel, not after another Fable handoff.

CONTINUE THE CONNECTED PURCHASING BUILD NOW. Keep the delivered work (do not rebuild the port, webhook processor, continuation components or execution store). Latest inspected source: d0d60960aa50791a829eb5cfde4050deee0b5c72. Read newer ownership and source once; preserve subsequent fixes.

FABLE — NEXT IMPLEMENTATION: continue the durable checkout submission path, but close these findings first, before mounting the composition. Coordinate exact ownership with A; if A is already correcting the SQL, Fable gives A the regression requirements and keeps building the disjoint submission/client integration. No concurrent edits.
1. PAYMENT RETRY RETENTION: the no-reference reconciliation path unconditionally retries creation with the original key. Add persisted first-attempt information and a provider-policy-bound retry check (Stripe removes idempotency keys after >= 24 h; reusing a pruned key creates a new request). An old uncertain attempt with no reference must not blindly create another payment. Injected clock; test the boundary, lost responses, known-reference recovery and concurrent retries. Preserve uncertainty.
2. EXECUTION IDENTITY: protect price_version and reservation_ids from uncontrolled mutation; verify the rest of the commercial identity and permitted phase transitions. No new organization/pricing/order authority.
3. RESERVATION COMPLETENESS: commit_captured must verify the complete expected reservation set and canonical order relationship, not merely update whichever rows still match status=held. Cover missing, released, expired, duplicate and already-finalized reservations per the actual reservation schema. If capture exists but local commit cannot complete, preserve the captured/reconciliation state and prevent premature fulfillment; a database failure does not undo an external charge.
4. CANCELLATION SETTLEMENT: connect commitCancelled to the actual cancellation/recovery path; do not return final completion merely because the provider phase became cancelled. Prove order cancellation and hold release happen once and recover after a crash between provider cancellation and local settlement.
5. DOWNSTREAM ORDER PROCESSING: identify the canonical outbox or equivalent durable mechanism (the coordinator contract mentions it; the candidate SQL inserts none). Reuse an existing verified mechanism if present; otherwise implement the required transactional entry. No duplicate fulfillment/notification queues.
SUBMISSION PATH: resolve buyer and eligibility server-side; validate canonical quote, price version, quantities, address/agreements, serviceability; persist canonical order, reservations and recoverable execution intent through the correct transactional boundary BEFORE any provider effect; bind retries to the same logical request and reject changed details; return execution request key, order reference, truthful state; mount the existing payment-authentication step and guarded continuation; reconcile provider truth before reporting success; connect the completed order to customer account and operations view. Do not turn on the production provider resolver as a shortcut.

A — START IN PARALLEL: review the actual SQL (supabase/candidates/20260909150000_research_checkout_executions.sql) against current orders, reservations, credit, events and migration history NOW; coordinate the fixes above; then run the corrected migration and actual database tests in the authorized staging scope, exercising the Supabase adapter and SQL functions (not only the in-memory store): first application against the representative baseline; documented rerun behaviour without duplicate history; full capture commit and rollback of a failed local transaction; concurrent orders competing for inventory and store credit; complete reservation validation; cancellation settlement and restart recovery; correct privileges and unavailable-database refusal; durable downstream processing without duplicate effects. No production migration replay, no shared-staging reset. If payment test effects fall outside existing permission, request that exact scope once while local implementation continues. Contract check for A: identify the actual durable downstream (outbox) mechanism rather than assuming the state-event row suffices.

B — INDEPENDENT REVIEW: review the integrated successor and the actual managed results; prioritize money, reservation, credit, cancellation and retry invariants; return a scoped acceptance or concrete findings; do not self-accept authored changes.

CONNECTED QUALIFICATION (after the corrected database composition works): provider sandbox/test-mode journey with approved identities and effects — ordinary payment, authentication-required payment, decline, duplicate submission, lost response, restart recovery, webhook redelivery (use the provider's documented duplicate/out-of-order behaviour), cancellation; reconcile provider records with execution, order, inventory and credit records; keep test mode explicit. No live charge, refund, customer notification or shipment is authorized by this coding instruction. Manual ordering keeps running meanwhile.

DELIVER AND CONTINUE: checkpoint fixes and integration units early; one writer per path; one heavy integrated run per shared host; no waiting on relay acknowledgments when disjoint work is ready; no repeating completed privacy/QR/Resource Hub work. A remains integration owner and sole production executor; after required review and connected qualification, A executes the pinned release/activation plan under the authentic standing authorization.

NEXT RESULT: corrected source; database rehearsal outcome; connected provider-test result; independent verdict; exact remaining deployment prerequisite.

FABLE STATUS: closing findings 1-4 now on my branch (port retention check with injected clock + persisted first-attempt stamp; trigger covers price_version/reservation_ids; commit_captured validates the full reservation set against order lines and records a local-commit failure while keeping the capture evidence; coordinator settles cancelled via commitCancelled with a settled marker and a cancel entry point). Finding 5: the canonical downstream today is enqueue-after-commit through the existing durable notification outbox (createOutboxLegacyOrderNotifier, deterministic unique event keys); I will wire the durable submission to it rather than add SQL outbox rows unless A finds a trigger-based mechanism. A: if you start editing the candidate SQL yourself, say so once and I will send you the regression requirements instead of pushing SQL changes.
